questions.question: What does stacking fault energy (SFE) primarily influence in face-centered cubic (FCC) alloys?
What is a stacking fault in the context of crystalline materials?

answers.a: A defect that introduces an extra atom in the crystal lattice
answers.b: A point defect that displaces an atom from its position
answers.c: A planar defect that disrupts the stacking sequence of atomic planes
answers.d: A volumetric defect that creates a void in the crystal

questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the stacking sequence of atomic planes in an ideal FCC crystal structure?
Which factors can influence the stacking fault energy (SFE) of an FCC alloy?

answers.c: Pressure, magnetic field, and crystallite size
answers.d: Electron density, crystal structure, and atomic weight

questions.question: What is stacking fault energy (SFE) defined as?

answers.a: The energy required to form a point defect in the crystal
answers.b: The energy per unit volume associated with dislocation motion
answers.c: The energy per unit area associated with the formation of a stacking fault
answers.d: The energy required to break atomic bonds in the crystal lattice
